literal_source_claim_en: A new proof of the Four-Colour Theorem.
statement_blocker: The catalog names an RSST proof and gives only the gloss 'a new proof of the Four-Colour Theorem.' It does not decide whether the exact root is the ordinary Four-Colour conclusion, that conclusion with required RSST provenance, the reducibility and unavoidability clause suite, a correctness theorem for the configuration/rule/program corpus, the quadratic algorithm, or an exact conjunction. Selecting the ordinary theorem alone would erase the proof-route identity and silently overlap THM-M-0833. Accountable and independent review must redirect the H5 proof-family label to one stable proposition or provenance package and freeze every graph, planarity, configuration, discharging, computation, algorithm, binder, hypothesis, conclusion, and boundary convention.
target_decision: hold ordinary theorem execution at H5 until accountable review redirects the proof-family label to a stable proposition or provenance-sensitive package without borrowing THM-M-0833, THM-M-0836, or THM-M-0838
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected root must fix finite graph and embedding types; vertex, edge, face, colour, configuration, ring, rule, program, certificate, and algorithm input/output types; all universes; and all finiteness, decidability, planarity, connectivity, and computation structures.
conclusion: Open: candidate conclusions include ordinary vertex-four-colourability, absence or existence of a good configuration under source-specific hypotheses, verified correctness of the RSST computational corpus and composition, or total correctness and quadratic complexity of a four-colouring algorithm.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition has been selected; statement review must resolve every listed boundary case.
candidate_scope_not_credited: every finite loopless planar graph admits a proper vertex-colouring with at most four colours
the ordinary Four-Colour conclusion with a required source-faithful RSST proof and computation provenance
announcement clause (2.2): no good configuration appears in a minimal counterexample
announcement clause (2.3): every internally 6-connected triangulation contains a good configuration
the conjunction of the minimal-counterexample reduction, clauses (2.2) and (2.3), and their composition to the Four-Colour Theorem
correctness and completeness of the 633-configuration reducibility corpus and the 32-rule unavoidability corpus with programs, data, certificates, and trust boundary
a total-correctness and quadratic-complexity theorem for the RSST four-colouring algorithm

loops, parallel edges, bridges, isolated vertices, finite versus infinite inputs, and at-most-four versus exactly-four colour conventions

program nontermination, parser rejection, integer overflow, compiler/runtime/hardware faults, certificate incompleteness, and checker trust
